tossups.text: This structure's medial section is known as the fasciculus grascillis, and one of its posterior projections contains the Substantia gelatinosa. Renshaw cells interconnect various cells in this structure, which develops in the embryo via the action of Sonic hedgehog on the basal plate. The dorsal root ganglia are located adjacent to this structure, whose ventral horn contains motor neuron afferents and whose injury can lead to tetraplegia or paraplegia. For 10 points, name this collection of nerves which make up the CNS with the brain and which are surrounded by vertebra, originating from the embryonic notochord.

This goddess's husband pushed a boulder to block the entrance of the underworld after she sent the God of Storms to chase him. As this goddess's son couldn't stand, he was sent to sea on a boat of reeds and became the god of luck and fishermen. This goddess's husband performed a cleansing ritual after seeing this her maggot-covered body in the underworld. Her son's deformity was due to this goddess speaking first after meeting her mate on the other side of the Pillar of Heaven. With her male counterpart, this goddess used the heavenly spear to churn the ocean and create Onogoroshima island. For 10 points, name this Japanese goddess of creation and death, the wife of Izanagi.

Some diseases of this organ may cause the formation of spiral-shaped mucus casts called Curschmann's spirals. A common side effect of prolonged treatment with busulfan is interstitial fibrosis in this organ. Like the liver, this organ can be damaged by genetic deficiency of a serine peptidase inhibitor called alpha-1 antitrypsin. A tumor in the upper part of this organ can result in anhidrosis and ipsilateral ptosis (TOH-siss) in Horner's syndrome. An elevated CD4/CD8 ratio in a fluid collected from this organ can be indicative of sarcoidosis. This organ's function can be plotted in flow-volume loops, which can help characterize obstructive and restrictive disorders in this organ. NRDS can be caused by the inability of newborns to produce surfactants in this organ. For 10 points, name this organ that facilitates gas exchange during breathing.

E.T.A. Hoffman said that this work "awakens that endless longing which is the essence of Romanticism." The bassoon and cello play a quiet, detached recapitulation of this symphony's third movement scherzo and trio. A lyrical oboe cadenza interrupts the recapitulation of the C minor Allegro con Brio first movement of this symphony, whose finale concludes by accelerating towards 29 bars of fortissimo C major chords. "Fate knocking at the door" describes the opening short short short long motif of, for 10 points, which of Ludwig van Beethoven's symphonies?

In one poem, Gary Snyder wrote that Philip Whalen had "built a poem" to this man and that the "drunkard [had] taught him how to dance." A poem titled "Thinking of" this poet "at the End of the Sky" asks "what thoughts occupy the gentleman's mind?" and "what time will the wild goose come?" One translation of this poet describes how the title character "played about the front gate, pulling flowers" when her husband returned and remembers "When my hair was cut straight across my forehead." That poem was translated as "The River Merchant's Wife: A Letter" by Ezra Pound. This poet wrote "A cup of wine, under the flowering trees" in "Drinking Alone by Moonlight." For 10 points, name this poet, who with Wang Wei and Du Fu, is among the most celebrated poets of the Tang Dynasty.

On a trip abroad, an asexual director from this country posed for a picture on a large phallic spiny cactus. In a film by Peter Greenaway, that director from this country has an affair with a guide giving him a tour of the Guanajuato Mummies. A director from this country opened a film with a minute-long low-angle shot of a cross overlooking the Atlantic Ocean. After a funeral procession emerges from between two burning cars in that film, its director from this country had the camera dolly out a window underneath a flag hoisted by factory workers. In a scene by a director from this country that inspired a Boogie Nights shot, the camera follows a bikini contest participant underwater in a rooftop swimming pool. Charlie Chaplin helped a director from this country meet Upton and Mary Sinclair to make the unfinished epic film ¡Que viva México! For 10 points, Soy Cuba is a film made by a crew from what home country of Sergei Eisenstein?

This city's Checkerboard Hill was used as a landmark for pilots approaching its old airport's Runway 13. This city is the eastern endpoint of the world's longest sea-crossing bridge. The longest escalator system in the world is this city's Central-Mid-Levels Escalator. This city's Mass Transit railway and its double-decker trams, which connect its Happy Valley to Causeway Bay, both use Octopus cards. Blue taxis are limited to Lantau Island in this city, which replaced the dangerous Kai Tak airport with one built on reclaimed land that is the main hub of Cathay Pacific. The main part of this city is connected by rail to Kowloon and the New Territories across the Pearl River Delta. For 10 points, name this Chinese Special Administrative Region connected by bridge to Macau.

In information retrieval, this function's namesake similarity is a common method of quantifying how well documents are related. The Dottie number is this function's unique real fixed point. This function is used in the real parts of both De Moivre's formula and Euler's formula. When graphed, an analogue of this function forms a catenary curve. The dot product of two vectors multiplies those vectors' norms by this function of the angle between them. When a, b, and c are the sides of a triangle, the fact that "c-squared equals a-squared plus b-squared minus two-ab times this function of the angle opposite c" is known as the law of this function. For 10 points, name this function whose reciprocal is secant, defined as adjacent over hypotenuse.
acceptableAnswers: accept answers like cosine of x

tossups.text: Under Dwight Eisenhower, this position was held by James Hagerty. The first man to hold it was Stephen Early, who took the job in 1937 and stayed with it for eight years. More recently, it has been held by Marlin Fitzwater, Mike McCurry, and Ari Fleischer. For 10 points, name this position in the executive branch held by Scott McClellan until he was replaced in 2006 by Tony Snow.

A reservoir in this state, which flooded the former villages of Ashland and Kent, supplies sixty percent of its drinking water. In 2011, its city of Central Falls declared bankruptcy and has contemplated merging with its southern neighbor, whose namesake "Falls" mark the boundary between the estuarine Seekonk and the Blackstone River. This home of Scituate Reservoir is also home to a city which was the epicenter of the colonial slave trade and whose "cottages" include Land's End and The Breakers. Pawtucket is found in this state, whose Aquidneck Island is home to Newport and is situated in Narragansett Bay. For 10 points, what Ocean State is the smallest by area in the U.S., and has its capital at Providence?

This astronomer described how nesting the Platonic solids within spheres could model the six known planets of the solar system. This author of Mysterium Cosmographicum argued that, during equal intervals of time, planets sweep out equal portions of their elliptical orbits. Data collected by Tycho Brahe was used by, for 10 points, what German astronomer who devised three laws of planetary motion?

From his work with Simon Kuznets, this man concluded that people make anticipated decisions based on economic factors in the future, a phenomenon which he termed the permanent-income hypothesis. This critic of the QE approach proposed that money should be injected straight into a community via a metaphorical "helicopter." Along with Edmund Phelps, this man criticized the model put forth by the Phillips curve, instead supporting the theory that there exists a "natural rate of unemployment." This man proposed a policy in which the central bank of a country should increase the money supply each year at a constant rate, which he dubbed his "k-percent rule." This man advised Augusto Pinochet, and served as an economic advisor to Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan. For 10 points, name this monetarist member of the Chicago School of Economics.

this structure is essential for atp and muscle energy. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this contraction-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The contraction is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in atp and muscle energy.

tossups.text: A differential equation describing the distribution functions of these systems assumes the Boltzmann transport equation is collisionless. Stored energy in these substances can be released via magnetic reconnection. These substances, whose time evolution is described by the Vlasov equation, are treated as a fluid governed by the Navier-Stokes equations and Maxwell's equations in magnetohydrodynamics. These substances screen out electric fields up to their Debye ("duh-BYE") length. Alfvén ("alf-VANE") waves in these substances were proposed to explain the coronal heating problem. Most of the Sun's mass is, for 10 points, what highly ionized fourth state of matter?

This country lost control of the Banda Oriental following the Cisplatine War. The Duke of Caxias led this nation's forces to victory over Paraguay in the War of the Triple Alliance. Getulio Vargas ended "coffee with milk" politics in this nation and later established the an Estado Novo here. The Golden Law ended slavery in this nation. This country was led by Pedro II until his deposition in 1889. For 10 points, name this South American nation, formerly a colony of Portugal.

In an adaptation of one of this author's works, one character declares "There's a ship: the Black Freighter, with a skull on its masthead will be coming in." This playwright had characters verbalize their decision process to enhance the "distancing" or "alienation" effect. This author adapted a John Gay play in a work that includes songs like "Pirate Jenny" and "Mack the Knife." In the most famous play by this promoter of "epic theatre," the title characters Kattrin, Eilif, and Swiss Cheese all die in the Thirty Years' War. For 10 points, name this twentieth-century German playwright, who wrote The Threepenny Opera and Mother Courage and Her Children .

One character in this play was named after a seaside resort in Sussex. A servant in this play, who was once married due to a "misunderstanding", prepares cucumber sandwiches, which are eaten before guests arrive. The governess Miss Prism receives a handbag at the end of this play, and Lady Bracknell allows Gwendolen Fairfax to be engaged. Jack Worthing and Algernon Moncrieff both don the title name in, for 10 points, what "trivial comedy" by Oscar Wilde?

In a story by this author, a Norwegian fisherman recounts his brother's death during a hurricane near the island of Moskoe. This author quoted Joseph Glanvill to describe a woman's eyes as "more profound than the well of Democritus." The title woman of a story by this author, who writes a poem that mentions an orchestra "breathing fitfully" and how "the play is the tragedy, 'Man,'" resurrects through Lady Rowena after composing "The Conqueror Worm." This author of "A Descent into the Maelström" wrote a story depicting black velvet decor and scarlet windows in the seventh room of a building whose ebony clock chimes hourly, causing guests to stop dancing at a ball hosted by Prince Prospero. For 10 points, name this American author of "Ligeia" and "The Masque of the Red Death."

In one scene in this work, men sit around a fire watching a televised chase of a criminal come to a bloody end. Afterwards, a man is touched on the arm and told "welcome back from the dead" by Granger. The protagonist tries to communicate with his wife, but she is too involved with her TV "family." That protagonist's worldview changes after he meets Clarisse McClellan, and he escapes the city after killing Captain Beatty and the Mechanical Hound. For 10 points, name this novel by Ray Bradbury, where books are illegally read and hidden by firefighter Guy Montag.

The first example of this industry in the United States was located in Simsbury, Connecticut and one-thirtieth of the profits were granted to Yale University. The first steam engine imported to the Americas was used in this industry. Workers in this industry were the primary victims of the Italian Hall disaster while on strike in Michigan's Keweenaw Peninsula, also known as "this commodity" country. Daniel Jackling revolutionised this industry at Bingham Canyon with open-pit production. A 1983 strike in this industry in Arizona led to mass decertification of unions. William Clark, F. Augustus Heinze, and Marcus Daly were the "kings" of this industry and dominated the politics of Butte (byoot), Montana. For 10 points, name this industry once dominated by the Anaconda Company.

parts.text: Name this function, used in signal processing, which equals zero for x less than zero and one for x greater than zero.
The Heaviside function can be approximated using the hyperbolic variety of this function, which in Cartesian coordinates is equal to sine divided by cosine.
This other special function, equal to the infinite sum of cosines of various multiples of x, is notable for being continuous everywhere but differentiable nowhere.

bonuses.leadin: Its integral is known as the ramp function. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this theory that explains how everyone is able to learn grammar, given the relatively little information learned in school.
acceptableAnswers: but DO NOT REVEAL Plato’s Problem

parts.text: This man theorized the concept of universal grammar and created a namesake hierarchy of grammars. In his Syntactic Structures, he made up the grammatically correct but meaningless sentence, "Colorless green ideas sleep furiously."

Chomsky was influenced in his "poverty of the stimulus" argument by this philosopher's dialogue Menon, in which this philosopher observes that an uneducated servant understands geometry when talking with Socrates.

bonuses.leadin: [NOTE TO MODERATOR: do not read out the alternate answer of the first answerline unless necessary] This argument is based on the fact that we are never presented with negative evidence. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this process which was described by Witten and Sander in 1981 to describe irreversible colloidal cluster formation. It is not dominated by convection and describes such phenomenon as matter combining to form dust or dendrite crystals and electrodeposition.

One problem that diffusion-limited aggregation can model is Hele-Shaw flow, which is a type of incompressible and irrotational flow and thus has a potential function that satisfies this equation. Poisson's equation is a modification of this equation when the right hand side is not zero.

Diffusion-limited aggregation can also model dielectric breakdown, which is the formation of electrically conducting regions in insulators when exposed to strong examples of this phenomenon. This phenomenon changes the index of refraction linearly in the Pockels effect.

bonuses.leadin: This process generally modeled by using a random walk with particles sticking to each other and to a fixed seed particle. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these figures. Following the death of Alma Mahler's daughter Manon Gropius, Alban Berg dedicated his violin concerto "to the memory of" one of these figures.
Angel of Light is the seventh symphony by Einojuhani Rautavaara, a composer from this home country of Jean Sibelius.

Rautavaara's Angel of Dusk is a concerto for this instrument. Former BSO music director Serge Koussevitzky was a virtuoso of this instrument and wrote an F-sharp minor concerto that popularized it as a solo instrument.

bonuses.leadin: The final movement of a concerto titled for one of these figures "of Dusk" is titled "His Last Appearance" and is part of a "series" that includes a symphony titled for one of these figures "of Light." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author who wrote The Sea-Wolf and White Fang.
This dog is taken from his owner, Judge Miller, and shipped to the Klondike, where he becomes a sled dog in London's The Call of the Wild.
In this Jack London short story, which is also set in the Klondike, a man freezes to death after getting his feet in Henderson Creek because he is unable to perform the title action.

bonuses.leadin: In one novel by this author, Humphrey Van Weyden is put to work aboard the schooner Ghost, and in another, the titular canine defends Weedon Scott from an attack. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this wooden artwork whose one of whose wings depict Christ's Entry into Jerusalem. This altarpiece in the church of Saint James in Rothenberg is named for what's contained in the vial at its center.

A wing of Tilman Riemenschneider's Holy Blood Altarpiece depicts this scene. Giovanni Bellini's unusual version of this scene includes a staircase over a river and depicts Jesus in prayer on the Mount of Olives.
The windows of the Saint James church contain depictions of the life of this figure. The archangel Gabriel tells this woman that she is pregnant in many Annunciation scenes.

bonuses.leadin: This artwork's unusual depiction of The Last Supper features Judas at the center instead of Jesus Christ. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This river, which flows over Victoria Falls, rises in northwestern Zambia and flows into the Mozambique Channel. It makes up or crosses the borders of six countries, including Zambia and Zimbabwe.
This river flows through Ghana to the Gulf of Guinea. Its principal headstreams are the White and Black tributaries, flowing out of Burkina Faso, whose original name was given by this river.
This river begins in Angola before ending in the Kalahari Desert of Botswana, where it creates the world's largest inland delta.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about African rivers, for 10 points each.

parts.text: As MOFs are porous with high surface area at the nanoscale, hydrogen gas can be captured by them via this process, in which molecules attach to a solid surface. Don't confuse it with a very similar term with a one-letter difference.

Much research interest has centered on the ability of MOFs to capture this molecule. Because it is a greenhouse gas, there has been a heavy focus on carbon sequestration to reduce its atmospheric concentration.
Many MOFs exhibit this crystal structure, which has the centers of exactly eight atoms positioned at the corners of a cubic unit cell.This cubic crystal structure has one atom per unit cell.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer some questions about the growing field of metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs.

parts.text: Name this European royal house whose strategic marriages and inbreeding led to a namesake "jaw". Maria Theresa was the only female ruler of this House of Austria.

Habsburg state chancellor von Kaunitz orchestrated this reversal of alliances between the War of Austrian Succession and the Seven Years' War. This event was part of the stately quadrille and saw Austria's abandonment of the Anglo-Austrian Alliance.
The Anglo-Prussian alliance ultimately prevailed after this "great" Prussian king's victory at the Battle of Leuthen ensured Prussian control of Silesia.

bonuses.leadin: The Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 was an edict issued by a monarch of this royal house. For ten points each:

parts.text: Moundville and Cahokia were both constructed by a culture named for this river, which divides the Cahokia site in Illinois from St. Louis in Missouri.
The more elaborate Serpent Mound is located in the state named for this largest tributary of the Mississippi, which also flows past the Angel Mounds.
The mound builders existed as east as this state, where they built sites at Etowah and Ocmulgee.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about the geography of the remains of the North American mound builders.

parts.text: Name these organisms. Ocean acidification and rising ocean temperatures have caused "bleaching" in these organisms, which make up namesake reefs.

When corals are bleached, their skeleton, which is made of this compound, becomes exposed. This compound is also found in the shells of gastropods and crustaceans, and it's the primary component of limestone.
This other rock is primarily composed of calcium carbonate. This rock makes up the White Cliffs of Dover, and sticks of this rock are used to write on blackboards in classrooms.

bonuses.leadin: Very biodiverse marine ecosystems based on these organisms eventually develop into atolls surrounding a lagoon. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This MIT professor and left-wing thinker proposed the idea of universal grammar and coined the phrase "colorless green ideas sleep furiously" as a grammatically correct but nonsensical sentence.
In one work, Chomsky ridiculed the linguistic ideas of Beyond Freedom and Dignity and Verbal Behavior, both of which were written by this American psychologist and pioneer of operant conditioning.
Though their namesake term is a misnomer, this man and Benjamin Lee Whorf name a hypothesis which asserts that language shapes how people think of and judge the world.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following questions about important people in linguistics. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with intestinal enzymes.
What is the main function of the duodenum in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to intestinal enzymes.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name this virus. The largest ever outbreak of this filovirus struck the countries of Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia in 2013.
This other filovirus is named after the German city in which it first appeared in 1967. This virus is often transmitted through the bites of infected fruit bats.
Filoviruses like Ebola and Marburg are carried only by bats, primates, and these animals. These animals also name the H1N1 strand of the influenza virus.

bonuses.leadin: This virus was first identified in West Africa in 1976 and is thought to be transmitted by bats. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this group of exploring Norse seafarers, often depicted in modern culture as rampaging berzerkers who sacked European cities like Paris.
Viking expansion beyond Scandinavia included the founding of a permanent colony on Greenland by this father of Leif Erikson.
Leif Erikson's exploration included the founding of Vinland, which included a settlement at L'anse aux Meadows [lahnz oh meadows] in this modern Canadian island province.

bonuses.leadin: Ragnar Lodbrok was a legendary ruler of these people, who defeated Charles the Bald's army on the Seine River in 845 AD. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this author, who wrote about Thea Kronborg becoming a renowned opera singer in Dresden in her novel The Song of the Lark.
This most famous novel by Cather sees Jim Burden, a native of Black Hawk, Nebraska, develop a strong bond with the title Bohemian immigrant.

The title character of this Cather short story flees to New York after working at Carnegie Hall in Pittsburgh. However, when his father finds out, he throws himself in front of a train rather than going back.

bonuses.leadin: She wrote about Jean Marie Latour's attempts to bring a cathedral to Santa Fe in her novel Death Comes for the Archbishop. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this comedic play in which Algernon Moncrieff and Jack Worthing both adopt the same name in order to win the hearts of Cecily Cardew and Gwendolen Fairfax.
The Importance of Being Earnest was written by this Irish-born playwright who also wrote the novel The Picture of Dorian Gray.

After Algernon learns that Jack uses the name Ernest when in the city, he states that he always suspected Jack was an expert of this practice. Performing this practice means avoiding responsibilities by claiming to have an appointment with a fictional person.

bonuses.leadin: At the end of this play, Miss Prism admits to accidentally leaving a handbag containing a baby in Victoria Station. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel, whose murderous protagonist visits a two-dimensional building inhabited by detectives who think that people can turn into bicycles.
The Third Policeman was written by this Irish humorist, who also wrote the novel At Swim-Two-Birds.

At Swim-Two-Birds inspired Jamie O'Neill's 2011 novel At Swim, Two Boys, which was written in this style. This style focuses on the thoughts of characters and is used in novels like Ulysses and Mrs. Dalloway.

bonuses.leadin: This novel frequently references the theories of a physicist named De Selby, who believes that a complex enough arrangement of mirrors could allow someone to see into the past. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this collection of stories about animals that includes "Rikki-Tikki-Tavi". Mowgli and Baloo also appear in this collection.
The Jungle Book is by this author, who also wrote "The White Man's Burden."
In "Rikki-Tikki-Tavi," the title mongoose kills two of these animals, named Nag and Nagaina.

bonuses.leadin: This collection of stories includes the tiger Shere Khan. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this revolt against the rule of James II, led by a bastard son of Charles II.
Monmouth was defeated at this battle, which is often referred to as the last battle on English soil, when a nighttime surprise attack was ruined by an accidental pistol shot.

This man commanded the king's infantry at Sedgemoor, though he would go on to be instrumental in the success of the Glorious Revolution. More notably, he was the victor at Blenheim and Ramillies in the War of the Spanish Succession.

bonuses.leadin: In its aftermath, George Jeffreys killed a bunch of people by way of the Bloody Assizes. FTPE:
